extracted.intended_audience: New Zealand government agencies preparing regulatory proposals for Cabinet
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for agencies on meeting New Zealand Cabinet's regulatory impact analysis (RIA) requirements, including creating, quality-assuring, submitting and publishing Regulatory Impact Statements (RISs) via RIA Online.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit regulatory proposals via RIA Online
rubrics_metrics.description: When an agency works to make a regulatory change, they need to submit the details of their regulatory proposal to the Ministry of Regulation through RIA Online.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RIA Online is where you: create the proposal; complete a climate implications of policy assessment (CIPA), which is reviewed by the Ministry for the Environment; apply for an exemption from the impact analysis process, if eligible; and get confirmation of the process to follow when submitting your proposal to Cabinet. If you haven’t accessed RIA Online before, set up an account by emailing RIA.Online@regulation.govt.nz with subject 'RIA Agency Access Request'. Accounts can only be approved for people with a government email address ending with '.govt.nz'. If you have issues signing up, contact RIA.Team@regulation.govt.nz.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create a Regulatory Impact Statement (RIS) when required
rubrics_metrics.description: If the proposal is subject to RIA requirements and not suitable for an exemption, you must create a RIS to go with the Cabinet paper; the RIS summarises an agency's best advice to its Minister and Cabinet and is based on the findings of the regulatory impact analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are different templates agencies can use depending on what’s required; the Ministry will confirm which template is most appropriate and will also confirm the wording to include in the impact analysis part of the Cabinet paper and the appropriate quality assurance arrangements. RIA Online is designed for unclassified or in-confidence content; if your RIS involves sensitive content or a national security classification, contact RIA.Team@regulation.govt.nz for advice on submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent quality assurance before Cabinet submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Each RIS prepared as part of a regulatory proposal to Cabinet should be independently assessed before it’s submitted with a Cabinet paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All RISs are quality assured against the same four criteria (Complete; Convincing; Consulted; Clear and concise). The Ministry will confirm the appropriate quality assurance arrangements to make.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete
rubrics_metrics.description: Is all the necessary information in the Regulatory Impact Statement, as set out in the relevant template?

rubrics_metrics.name: Convincing
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the analysis accurate, robust and balanced?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Are the analysis and conclusions supported by the analytical framework, and a commensurate assessment of costs and benefits and supporting evidence? Do the assumptions make sense?

rubrics_metrics.name: Consulted
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the RIS show evidence of efficient and effective consultation with stakeholders, key affected parties and relevant experts?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Does it show how any issues raised have been addressed or dealt with?

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear and concise
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the material communicated in plain English and is the RIS an appropriate length?

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission to Cabinet (CabNet) with supporting documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Once completed, the RIS document is submitted to Cabinet along with the Cabinet paper, and any other documents required, via CabNet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Get information about CabNet from the Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publishing RIS documents
rubrics_metrics.description: RISs are published on both the authoring agency’s website and the Ministry's website at the same time as the relevant bill is introduced to Parliament or the regulation is gazetted, or at the time the material is proactively released.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In line with proactive release requirements, RISs generally need to be published within 30 business days of the proposal being considered by Cabinet. RISs should be submitted for publication through RIA Online. Making RISs available online supports open and transparent regulatory process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redaction and handling of sensitive information on publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Not all information in RIS documents is appropriate to release publicly; sensitive information will be withheld consistent with the Official Information Act 1982.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a RIS document includes redacted content, agencies should ensure the version submitted for publication through RIA Online matches the version published to their own website. For sensitive or national security classified material, contact RIA.Team@regulation.govt.nz for submission guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transition to Regulatory Analysis Summary from 1 July 2026
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirements for regulatory impact analysis will be changing on 1 July 2026 and new templates and guidance will be made available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If preparing to take a regulatory policy proposal to Cabinet on or after 1 July 2026, you will need to prepare a Regulatory Analysis Summary instead of a Regulatory Impact Statement. The requirements for regulatory proposals for Cabinet are set out in the Cabinet office circular CO(26)2 'Expectations for good law‑making'. Relevant RIS templates and guidance notes (including those produced by Treasury) are provided by the Ministry.
